title: 2018 AMC 8 Problem 24
statement: In the cube \(ABCDEFGH\) with opposite vertices \(C\) and \(E,\) \(J\) and \(I\) are the midpoints of edges \(\overline{FB}\) and \(\overline{HD},\) respectively. Let \(R\) be the ratio of the area of the cross-section \(EJCI\) to the area of one of the faces of the cube. What is \(R^2?\)

solutions.text: Allow \(s\) to represent the length of an edge of the cube. Noting that each side of the cross section is equal in length, we conclude that \(EJCI\) is a rhombus. The area of this rhombus can be calculated as \(\frac12 IJ\cdot CE,\) as the area of a rhombus is equal to half the product of its diagonals. Using the Pythagorean Theorem: \[IJ=FH=s\sqrt{2}.\] Similarly, using the Pythagorean Theorem again lets us see that: \[\begin{align*}CE&=\sqrt{AC^2+AE^2}\\&=\sqrt{(s\sqrt{2})^2+s^2}\\&=\sqrt{2s^2+s^2}\\&=s\sqrt{3}\end{align*}\] Therefore, \[\begin{align*}R&=\dfrac{\frac12 IJ\cdot CE}{s^2}\\&=\dfrac{\frac12 s^2\sqrt{2}\sqrt{3}}{s^2}\\&=\sqrt{\dfrac32}\end{align*}\] Thus, \(R^2=\dfrac32,\) and the correct answer is C.
hints: The quadrilateral \(EJCI\) is a rhombus, so use its diagonals.
Express the diagonals \(IJ\) and \(CE\) in terms of the cube side length.
